To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) honey bee workers live longer in smaller colonies; (2) this effect is independent of the age at which workers start foraging; (3) it occurs in both the in-hive stage and the foraging phase of workers; (4) it occurs independently of worker genotype; (5) large colonies grow faster, forage at higher rates, and raise more brood than small colonies.
“Individuals in larger honey bee colonies live shorter lives than individuals in smaller honey bee colonies.”
honey bee (Apis melliferia) workers live longer if they are reared in small colonies, independently of their age at the transition from the in-hive to the foraging stage.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the relation between individual longevity, social group size, and the growth of super-organisms, and it contributes to the understanding of the systemic aging of multi-cellular and super-organismic life forms.
the relation between colony size, longevity of individuals and life-history phases in honey bees, and the potential for this relation to inform our understanding of aging in multi-cellular organisms.
the relationship between colony growth and worker lifespan and the potential role of social environment in shaping this relationship.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lifespan of honey bee workers decreases with colony size, but that this effect is confounded by the effect of age at transition from in-hive to foraging activity.
social insect colonies are not super-organisms but rather that they are super-individuals.
social group size does not have a positive effect on longevity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the social insect colony can serve as a model for studying the relation between organismal and individual aging, as well as for studying the evolution of aging.
social insects, like other organisms, are not immortal.
the longevity of individual workers is negatively correlated with colony size, and that the age at first foraging determines the longevity of honey bee workers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
colony size is an important factor in the regulation of honey bee lifespan.
colony size is an important factor to take into consideration when investigating the effects of social environment on individual longevity.
social insects can serve as a model for studying aging in superorganisms.
